nodes.description: Fenestration is considered for accessible superficial large cysts; segmental resection can help severe disease clustered in selected segments with sufficient spared parenchyma and patent vasculature. These procedures carry morbidity, recurrence and possible difficulty at later transplantation. In the 186-patient combined resection/fenestration series, 170 had ADPKD and only 16 ADPLD; major complications occurred in 21% and 90-day mortality was 2.7%. Its durable median 61% volume reduction comes from selected patients at a single expert center, not a randomized comparison with transplantation.

nodes.description: Long-acting octreotide or lanreotide can modestly reduce or stabilize liver volume in symptomatic diffuse PLD. These uses remain off-label as described in the 2026 ERN statement. Assess symptoms and consistent volumetry over 6–12 months; response can include symptom relief with volume stabilization. Benefit can persist during ongoing treatment for several years, while withdrawal can cause rebound. Monitor gastrointestinal intolerance, glucose disturbance, gallstones, injection reactions and cyst infection. Advanced kidney disease requires individualized dosing and caution; avoid during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Pasireotide has more glucose toxicity and is not first-line. Volume reduction does not establish prevention of transplantation or renal functional decline.
